items.title: Today's lesson
items.content:
A cricket catch opens the lesson: why pull the hands back?

One cart on a smooth track carries the concept: **bigger pulls** give bigger accelerations, **more mass** gives smaller ones, and together they give **F = ma** and the **newton**.

The cart on a rough floor shows F is the **net force**; weight is **F = mg**; two carts tied together act as **one system**.

items.title: You already know
items.content:
• net force along a line; a net force changes velocity (Newton's first law)

• acceleration, a = (v − u) ÷ t, and the equations of motion

• the slope of a velocity–time graph gives the acceleration

items.title: By the end, you can
items.content:
**1.** State Newton's second law and define the newton.

**2.** Apply F = ma to solve numericals.

**3.** Calculate the acceleration of connected objects treated as one system.

**What this shows**

Readings for a **2 kg cart** pulled along a **smooth track** (no friction) with pulls of 2 N, 4 N and 6 N. The last acceleration is hidden.

**Answer to Question 4**

items.prompt: A net force gives a scooter an acceleration of 2 m/s². What is its acceleration if (i) the net force is tripled, (ii) the same force acts on the scooter with a rider, so the mass is doubled?
A ball is rolling to the east. The net force on it acts to the west. Its acceleration is
options: to the east, and it speeds up
to the east, and it slows down
to the west, and it slows down
zero, so its speed stays the same

items.text:
**On Question 2**

**B**: F = ma, so N = kg × m/s².

**On Question 3**

**C**: the acceleration is **along the net force**, to the west, opposite to the motion, so the ball **slows down**.

items.text:
**What this shows**

A **20 kg cart** pulled forwards with **70 N** along a **rough floor**; friction of **30 N** acts backwards.

**Answer to Question 10**

**Neither.** F is the **net force**: 70 N − 30 N = **40 N, forwards**.

**Answer to Question 11**

a = 40 ÷ 20 = **2 m/s², forwards**.

**Answer to Question 12**

s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½ × 2 × 3² = **9 m**.

items.prompt: A car of mass 1000 kg moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest in 5 s. Taking the direction of motion as positive, the braking force is
Fill in the blanks: A student of mass 50 kg has a weight of ____ N (g = 9.8 m/s²). Her mass is measured in ____ and her weight in ____.
A 40 kg box is pushed with 100 N, and friction of 20 N acts on it. Its acceleration is

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**B**: a = (0 − 20) ÷ 5 = −4 m/s²; F = 1000 × (−4) = −4000 N, so **4000 N, opposite to the motion**.

**On Question 2**

**C**: 50 × 9.8 = **490 N**. Mass in **kilograms**; weight is a force, in **newtons**.

**On Question 3**

**B**: net force = 100 − 20 = 80 N; a = 80 ÷ 40 = **2 m/s²**. (A) ignores friction.

items.text:
**What this shows**

(a) A **4 kg** cart and a **2 kg** cart tied with a string, pulled with **12 N** on a **smooth track**.

(b) The same carts with a **dashed line** drawn round both. Reveal it after Question 14.

**Answer to Question 13**

**Together.** They always have the same velocity, so the **same acceleration**.

**Answer to Question 14**

**The string.**

**Answer to Question 15**

2 kg + 4 kg = **6 kg**.

**Answer to Question 16**

**Only the 12 N pull.** The string is inside the object, joining one part to another.

**Answer to Question 17**

a = 12 ÷ 6 = **2 m/s²**, for **both** carts.

**Answer to Question 18**

4 × 2 = **8 N**. This is the **string's pull** on it.

items.prompt: A boy pulls two sledges of 10 kg and 15 kg, tied together, across smooth ice with a force of 50 N. Their acceleration and the net force on the 15 kg sledge are
True or false? To find the acceleration of the two sledges, we must add the pull of the rope between them to the boy's pull.
options: True: the rope pulls the 15 kg sledge forwards
True: both pulls act on the sledges
False: the rope's pull is internal to the system
False: the rope's pull is zero

items.text:
**On Question 1**

**A**: a = 50 ÷ (10 + 15) = **2 m/s²**; net force on the 15 kg sledge = 15 × 2 = **30 N**.

**On Question 2**

**C**: **false**. The rope's pull is **internal** to the system, so it is left out.
